goal: Test establishment/filtering across Izu pollinator-regime geography without treating public-record non-detection as biological absence.

candidate_sources.title: 伊豆諸島の植物誌 第4版
candidate_sources.coverage: Izu Islands flora; expected best candidate for a reviewed multi-island species matrix
candidate_sources.current_access: bibliographic metadata verified via National Diet Library search; species-by-island contents not recovered through the current public route
candidate_sources.next_action: obtain a lawful readable copy or structured transcription before any island-absence analysis

candidate_sources.title: On the Plant Distribution over Izu-Islands
candidate_sources.limitation: supports broad north/south floristic boundary context but is not treated here as a complete modern species-by-island establishment matrix

candidate_sources.title: An Annotated Checklist of the Vascular Plants of Aogashima Island in the Izu Islands, Japan
candidate_sources.limitation: single-island checklist cannot by itself support the nine-island transition comparison

explicitly_rejected_shortcuts: treat GBIF or iNaturalist non-detection as biological absence
combine unequal public-record effort into an uncorrected island presence/absence matrix
infer native establishment from occurrence coordinates alone
use the 1956 phytogeographic summary as if it were a complete species-by-island checklist
minimum_source_matrix_requirements: island-level established/present status from a reviewed flora or checklist
explicit source citation and locality scope
documented handling of historical versus contemporary status

planned_analysis_once_open.primary_question: Are source-resolved high pollinator-dependency mainland lineages less likely than broader-dependency lineages to persist as comparable established taxa across the Oshima/post-boundary geography after area isolation habitat/history controls?
planned_analysis_once_open.claim_boundary: Even a reviewed presence/absence matrix would test ecological filtering/establishment, not within-population floral evolution or historical pollinator causation.

claim_boundary: The occupancy workstream is intentionally blocked rather than substituting public-record zeros for absence. The current evidence supports a survivorship-selection concern but does not yet quantify its archipelago-wide magnitude.
